record.paper_title: Homogenization in mechanics. A survey of solved and open problems
record.original_question: How should homogenization account for initial stresses in composite elastic materials, such as stresses introduced by stretching some constituents during manufacture, when those initial stresses add to deformation-induced stresses and can affect whether local stress or strain reaches a fracture threshold?

artifact.category_tag: homogenization of elastic composites with initial stresses
artifact.status_search_result: Homogenization in the presence of initial/residual stresses has been studied for several decades. Asymptotic two-scale expansions yielding effective elastic moduli that depend on local initial stresses are known (e.g., Kalamkarov–Kolpakov type results, and book-length treatments of stressed composite thin-walled structures). Models for residual stresses in random elastic composites via nonlocal micromechanics, and homogenization of prestressed elastic lattices, have appeared. However, a fully general theory linking corrector-based local stress/strain reconstruction to pointwise fracture criteria in composites with arbitrary initial stresses remains an active research direction rather than a closed problem.
